usdRate.note: The Eastern Caribbean dollar has been fixed at EC$2.70 per US dollar by the ECCB since 1976.

inflation_cpi.sourceName: Statistics Division, Ministry of Finance and Corporate Governance: Consumer Price Index for September 2026 (release of 2 October 2026)
inflation_cpi.note: CPI rose 7.0% in the twelve months to September 2026 (1.1% in the month); the year-on-year rate climbed from 3.7% in June 2026, and was 3.1% in December 2025 (Statistics Division monthly inflation table).

inflation_projection.sourceName: Statistics Division monthly year-on-year CPI rates (2019-2026); EC dollar pegged to the US dollar at 2.70
inflation_projection.note: The ECCB has no inflation target but the fixed US-dollar peg anchors prices; year-on-year inflation swung between about -1% and 7% in 2025-2026 and averaged about 3% over the longer run, so we plan with 3% despite the September 2026 spike.

policy_rate.sourceName: Eastern Caribbean Central Bank, interest rates on deposits and loans (ECCB table, country Antigua and Barbuda)
policy_rate.note: ECCB discount rate for short-term credit 3.0%, unchanged through August 2026 in the ECCB table (Antigua and Barbuda selected).

savings_account_rate.sourceName: Eastern Caribbean Central Bank, interest rates and weighted average rates on deposits and loans (ECCB table, country Antigua and Barbuda)
savings_account_rate.note: Weighted average EC-dollar savings deposit rate 2.05%; quoted savings rates range 2.00-2.25%, and the ECCB minimum savings rate is 2%.

fdr_3m_rate.sourceName: Eastern Caribbean Central Bank, interest rates on deposits and loans (ECCB table, country Antigua and Barbuda)
fdr_3m_rate.note: 3-month EC-dollar time deposits quoted at 2.00% (minimum and maximum).

fdr_1y_rate.sourceName: Eastern Caribbean Central Bank, interest rates on deposits and loans (ECCB table, country Antigua and Barbuda)
fdr_1y_rate.note: 12-month EC-dollar time deposits quoted from 0.10% to 2.50% (August 2026); the weighted average on all EC-dollar time deposits was 1.87% (June 2026), so 2.0% is used as typical.

dps_rate.note: Searched ECCB interest rate tables: no monthly recurring deposit product rate is published for Antigua and Barbuda.

bank_deposit_avg_rate.sourceName: Eastern Caribbean Central Bank, interest rates and weighted average rates on deposits and loans (ECCB table, country Antigua and Barbuda)
bank_deposit_avg_rate.note: Weighted average rate on all EC-dollar deposits 1.32% in June 2026 (1.17% including foreign-currency deposits).

sanchayapatra_5y_rate.note: No government savings certificate or retail savings bond for individuals found for Antigua and Barbuda; government securities are sold by auction on the Regional Government Securities Market.

tbill_91d_rate.note: The Government of Antigua and Barbuda issued no 91-day bills in 2025-2026; its latest bills were 180-day at 3.00% (July 2026) and 365-day at 4.50% (September 2026), per the ECCB RGSM weighted average rates table.

tbond_5y_rate.note: No 5-year Antigua and Barbuda bond auctioned on the RGSM in 2025-2026; the ECCB RGSM table shows only a 2-year bond at 4.00% (May 2026) and a 3-year bond at 5.80% (September 2025).

tbond_10y_rate.note: No 10-year Antigua and Barbuda bond auctioned on the RGSM in 2025-2026 per the ECCB RGSM weighted average rates table.

tax_bank_interest.sourceName: Caribbean Journal (news): Antigua and Barbuda abolishes personal income tax
tax_bank_interest.note: Personal income tax was abolished from April 2016, so resident individuals pay no tax on bank interest (a withholding tax applies to non-residents). Secondary source from 2016 (older than 2025); the Inland Revenue Department's list of taxes (October 2026) still shows no personal income tax.

tax_sanchayapatra_profit.note: No government savings certificate for individuals exists to tax; resident individuals pay no income tax on investment income since 2016.

deposit_insurance_limit.note: The Eastern Caribbean Deposit Insurance Corporation Agreement (signed 2025) is being enacted by ECCU members, but no operating scheme or coverage limit for Antigua and Barbuda could be confirmed.

credit_card_rate_cap.note: No legal cap or published typical credit card rate found; ECCB tables give only 'other lending rates' of 4-24% for Antigua and Barbuda.

equity_return_low.sourceName: No liquid local equity index; global equities in EC-dollar (US-dollar-pegged) terms
equity_return_low.note: Low case close to the 3-4.5% government bill yields, for a weak decade in global markets.

equity_return_base.sourceName: No liquid local equity index; global equities in EC-dollar terms; 365-day T-bill 4.50% (Sep 2026)
equity_return_base.note: The regional exchange lists only a handful of thinly traded shares, so equity is a global index fund in EC-dollar terms at about 6.5%, within 4 points of the untaxed 4.5% 1-year government bill rate.

equity_return_high.note: High case if global equities repeat their long-run record of about 9% a year in US dollars.

gold_return_low.sourceName: EC dollar fixed at 2.70 per US dollar (World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF)
gold_return_low.note: Low case: weak dollar gold prices with no currency depreciation under the peg.

gold_return_base.sourceName: EC dollar fixed at 2.70 per US dollar (World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF)
gold_return_base.note: Long-run dollar gold trend of about 4-5% with no expected EC-dollar depreciation under the peg.

gold_return_high.sourceName: EC dollar fixed at 2.70 per US dollar (World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF)
gold_return_high.note: High case with strong dollar gold prices.

fixed_income_return_low.sourceName: ECCB: savings and 3-month deposits about 2.0% (ECCB table, country Antigua and Barbuda)
fixed_income_return_low.note: Low case: savings and short deposits at the 2% minimum savings rate; no tax on resident interest.

fixed_income_return_base.sourceName: ECCB: 12-month deposits up to 2.5%; 180-day T-bills 3.00% and 365-day 4.50% (ECCB table, country Antigua and Barbuda)
fixed_income_return_base.note: Base case mixing 1-year deposits and government bills, untaxed for residents.

fixed_income_return_high.note: High case: holding 1-year government bills and short bonds at about 4-4.5%.

life_claim_settlement_rate.note: Searched the Financial Services Regulatory Commission's material: no industry-wide life claim settlement ratio published.

insurance_term_premium_table.note: Term life cover is sold in Antigua and Barbuda, but no regulator or other non-company source publishes premium rates by age.

health_hospitalisation_cost.note: No published typical cost of a major private hospital stay found for Antigua and Barbuda.

health_premium_table.note: No regulator or other non-company source publishing private health insurance premiums by age found.

goal_inflation_health.sourceName: ECCB CPI table, Antigua and Barbuda health sub-index (2018 100.1, 2025 114.3)
goal_inflation_health.note: The health index rose about 2% a year over 2018-2025 but swings widely, so we plan with the 3% headline projection plus one point for imported medical costs.

goal_inflation_education.sourceName: ECCB CPI table, Antigua and Barbuda education sub-index (2018 100.0, 2025 114.9)
goal_inflation_education.note: The education index averaged about 2% a year over 2018-2025 but jumped 13% in 2025, so we plan with the headline projection plus half a point.

life_expectancy.note: UN WPP 2024 (via populationpyramid.net) gives 78.1 for 2026 (men 75.1, women 80.7).

life_table_remaining.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects 2024 via populationpyramid.net
life_table_remaining.note: Secondary source of UN WPP 2024 medium variant for 2026; totals at 60, 70 and 80 are the mean of men and women (only the 65 total is published there).

support_ratio.sourceName: World Bank SP.POP.DPND.OL (2025); UN WPP 2024 via populationpyramid.net (2040, 2065)
support_ratio.note: 100 / old-age dependency ratio: 17.6 (2025, World Bank), 32.4 (2040) and 53.5 (2065, populationpyramid.net/antigua-and-barbuda/2065/).

retirement_age_default.sourceName: Antigua and Barbuda Social Security Board: media release on pension and contribution rate adjustments
retirement_age_default.note: Social security pensionable age moved to 65 on 1 January 2025 (Statutory Instrument 2016 No. 61), the end of the phased rise from 60; there is no separate statutory private-sector retirement age.

retirement_age_government.note: Public officers historically retired at 60; a 2019-2020 bill to raise the public service retirement age to 65 was reported, but its enactment could not be confirmed from an official source.

retirement_return_low.sourceName: ECCB: savings and 3-month deposits about 2.0% (ECCB table, country Antigua and Barbuda)
retirement_return_low.note: Low case: savings and short deposits, untaxed for residents.

retirement_return_base.sourceName: ECCB: 12-month deposits up to 2.5%; 365-day T-bill 4.50% (ECCB table, country Antigua and Barbuda)
retirement_return_base.note: Base case below the 4.5% 1-year government bill rate, mixing deposits and bills.

retirement_return_high.note: High case: mostly 1-year government bills and short bonds.

retirement_accumulation_return_low.sourceName: Mix of EC-dollar deposits/bills (2-4.5%) and global equities
retirement_accumulation_return_low.note: Low case for a balanced mix in a weak decade.

retirement_accumulation_return_base.sourceName: Mix of EC-dollar deposits/bills (2-4.5%) and global equities (6.5% base)
retirement_accumulation_return_base.note: Base case for a roughly half-and-half mix of safe EC-dollar assets and global equities.

retirement_accumulation_return_high.sourceName: Mix of EC-dollar bills and global equities (9% high case)
retirement_accumulation_return_high.note: High case with a strong equity decade.

old_age_allowance_monthly.note: The only non-contributory old-age pension, the Old-age Assistance Programme (EC$255 a month), is limited to people who were 65 or older in 1993 (or blind or disabled), so no one planning today can receive it (UN ECLAC non-contributory programmes database, https://dds.cepal.org/bpsnc/programme?id=145).

old_age_allowance_eligibility.note: No old-age assistance open to new claimants: the Old-age Assistance Programme covers only people who were 65 or older in 1993 (UN ECLAC non-contributory programmes database, https://dds.cepal.org/bpsnc/programme?id=145).

gratuity_rule.note: No statutory retirement gratuity found; the Labour Code's severance pay applies only on redundancy or dismissal after a year of service, and the official text of the Code could not be read to confirm the scale.

public_pension_scheme.sourceName: Antigua and Barbuda Social Security Board: Age Benefit
public_pension_scheme.note: Compulsory social security for employees and the self-employed: age pension from 65 of 25% of average insurable earnings (best 5 of the last 10 years) for the minimum contributions plus 1% per 50 further weekly contributions, up to 50%; minimum EC$350 a month; a lump-sum age grant if fewer contributions; early claims cut 0.5% a month. No automatic indexation found; pensions are untaxed since personal income tax was abolished.

dps.note: No standard monthly recurring deposit product rate published for Antigua and Barbuda.

sanchayapatra_5y.note: No government savings certificate or retail savings bond for individuals found.

tbill_91d.localNameEn: Government of Antigua and Barbuda Treasury bill (180 or 365 days)
tbill_91d.note: Sold by auction on the Regional Government Securities Market through licensed intermediaries; recent issues are 180-day and 365-day bills, not 91-day.

tbond_5y.note: No 5-year government bond auctioned on the RGSM in 2025-2026; only 2- and 3-year bonds.

tbond_10y.note: No 10-year government bond auctioned on the RGSM in 2025-2026.

equity_fund.note: No locally registered retail mutual or index fund market found; the regional securities exchange lists only a few thinly traded shares.

gold.note: No legal restriction on buying gold; mainly sold as jewellery.

insuranceComplaints.name: Financial Services Regulatory Commission (FSRC)
insuranceComplaints.note: No separate insurance ombudsman found; complaints go to the insurer, then the FSRC.

pensionScheme.name: Antigua and Barbuda Social Security Board (age benefit)

publicHealthCover.name: Medical Benefits Scheme
publicHealthCover.note: Payroll-funded scheme covering treatment for listed conditions; public hospital care is subsidised.
